title: ggplot2 basics: bar and column charts
explanation: **Welcome to Level 6: charts with ggplot2!** You made your first charts back in Level 1. Now you'll build real, readable charts. Remember the recipe: `ggplot(data, aes(x = ..., y = ...)) + geom_...()`. A very common pattern is to **summarise first** with dplyr, then pipe the summary straight into ggplot.

tasks.prompt: Count the movies per genre with geom_bar(): ggplot(box_office, aes(x = genre)) + geom_bar().
hints: geom_bar() counts rows, so it only needs x.

tasks.teach: You can pipe a table straight into **ggplot()**. Careful: dplyr steps join with `|>`, but ggplot layers join with **`+`**. Mixing them up is the most common ggplot error.
tasks.prompt: Now show total gross per genre. Summarise first, then pipe into ggplot with geom_col(): box_office |> group_by(genre) |> summarize(total = sum(gross)) |> ggplot(aes(x = genre, y = total)) + geom_col().
hints: When you pipe into ggplot, leave the data out of ggplot(): it comes through the pipe.
Notice the switch from |> to + once you're inside ggplot.
tasks.answer: box_office |> group_by(genre) |> summarize(total = sum(gross)) |> ggplot(aes(x = genre, y = total)) + geom_col()

tasks.teach: **reorder(category, value)** sorts the bars from smallest to largest value, so the ranking jumps out.
tasks.prompt: Bars in A to Z order are hard to read. Sort them by size: change x to reorder(genre, total).
hints: reorder(column, value) orders the categories by the value.
tasks.answer: box_office |> group_by(genre) |> summarize(total = sum(gross)) |> ggplot(aes(x = reorder(genre, total), y = total)) + geom_col()

tasks.teach: **fill** colours the inside of bars by a column. ggplot adds a legend automatically and stacks the colours in each bar.
tasks.prompt: Last one: colour each bar by rating, with fill. Count movies per genre again, with fill = rating inside aes(): ggplot(box_office, aes(x = genre, fill = rating)) + geom_bar().
hints: ggplot(box_office, aes(x = genre, fill = rating)) + geom_bar()
tasks.answer: ggplot(box_office, aes(x = genre, fill = rating)) + geom_bar()

recap: geom_bar() counts rows, and geom_col() draws values you've summarised. Pipe a dplyr summary into ggplot, switching from |> to +. reorder() sorts bars, and fill colours them by a column.
